name: Question 15
problem:
Consider the inhomogeneous system  ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x({t}_{0})$ is presented below.

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let $y(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)$  

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${y}^{′}(t)=-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}{x}^{′}(t)$  

$\text{L3}:\,$ ${y}^{′}(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t)$  

$\text{L4}:\,$ $y(t)-y({t}_{0})={\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $y({t}_{0})=x({t}_{0})$ 

$\text{L6}:\,$ $y(t)=x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s$  

$\text{L7}:\,$ ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t)=x(t)$

$\text{L9}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from $\text{L3}$ by  
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from line $\text{L1}$ by  
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ follows from line $\text{L1}$ by  
{{field-3}}.
worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\text{L3}$ and $\text{L4}.$ Integrating ${y}^{′}(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t)$ from ${t}_{0}$ to $t$ in $\text{L3}$ yields

$$
y(t)-y({t}_{0})={\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s.
$$

Thus, $\text{L4}$ follows from $\text{L3}$ by $\text{integrating both sides from }{t}_{0}\text{ to }t.$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L5}.$ Evaluating $y(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)$ at $t={t}_{0}$ gives

$$
y({t}_{0})={e}^{-A({t}_{0}-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})=Ix({t}_{0})=x({t}_{0}).
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by $\text{evaluating at }t={t}_{0}.$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L8}.$ Multiplying both sides of

$$
y(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)
$$

from $\text{L1}$ by ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t) & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t) \\  & =x(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by $\text{multiplying both sides by }{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}.$

html:
Question 15
?
Consider the inhomogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t)+g(t), where A is a constant square matrix. A derivation of the formula for the solution x(t) passing through x(t0) is presented below.

L1: Let y(t)=e−A(t−t0)x(t)

L2: y′(t)=−Ae−A(t−t0)x(t)+e−A(t−t0)x′(t)

L3: y′(t)=e−A(t−t0)g(t)

L4: y(t)−y(t0)=∫t0te−A(s−t0)g(s)ds

L5: y(t0)=x(t0)

L6: y(t)=x(t0)+∫t0te−A(s−t0)g(s)ds

L7: eA(t−t0)y(t)=eA(t−t0)x(t0)+∫t0teA(t−s)g(s)ds

L8: eA(t−t0)y(t)=x(t)

L9: x(t)=eA(t−t0)x(t0)+∫t0teA(t−s)g(s)ds

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

Line L4 follows from L3 by
integrating both sides from t0 to t
multiplying both sides by eA(t−t0)
evaluating at t=t0
applying a change of variables
integrating both sides from t0 to t
.

Line L5 follows from line L1 by
evaluating at t=t0
multiplying both sides by eA(t+t0)
differentiating and using the sum rule
multiplying both sides by eA(t−t0)
evaluating at t=t0
.

Line L8 follows from line L1 by
multiplying both sides by eA(t−t0)
multiplying both sides by eA(t+t0)
multiplying both sides by eA(t−t0)
differentiating and using the sum rule
evaluating at t=t0
.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's justify each of the selected steps.

  • We first consider lines L3 and L4. Integrating y′(t)=e−A(t−t0)g(t) from t0 to t in L3 yields
    y(t)−y(t0)=∫t0te−A(s−t0)g(s)ds.
    Thus, L4 follows from L3 by integrating both sides from t0 to t.

  • Next, we consider lines L1 and L5. Evaluating y(t)=e−A(t−t0)x(t) at t=t0 gives
    y(t0)=e−A(t0−t0)x(t0)=Ix(t0)=x(t0). Therefore, L5 follows from L1 by evaluating at t=t0.

  • Finally, we consider lines L1 and L8. Multiplying both sides of y(t)=e−A(t−t0)x(t) from L1 by eA(t−t0) gives
    eA(t−t0)y(t)=eA(t−t0)e−A(t−t0)x(t)=x(t). Therefore, L8 follows from L1 by multiplying both sides by eA(t−t0).
